items.title: Snow Disrupts Austria
items.gist: A heavy first snowfall brought winter into the commute all at once. Roads, trains and flights faced delays, and emergency crews were busy.
items.summary: Heavy snow fell across many parts of Austria on Thursday. The A21 motorway near Vienna was closed after vehicles became stuck. Traffic was also disrupted in Vienna, Tirol and Kärnten. In Kärnten, about 8,000 homes temporarily lost power. Authorities warned that snow and icy roads could cause more delays. Road and winter-service teams worked to clear routes and assist people.
items.host_open: Austria woke to a very different commute today. How did the snow affect your plans?

items.title: Vienna Cuts Culture Budget
items.gist: The city plans to save €31 million in its cultural budget next year. Arts groups are questioning what those cuts could mean for venues and programmes.
items.summary: Vienna plans to save €31 million in its cultural budget for 2027. City culture councillor Veronica Kaup-Hasler announced the planned savings on Thursday. The cuts come as the city prepares its next budget. The announcement has drawn criticism from people in the cultural sector. They have called for more understanding of the effects on cultural work. The city has not yet detailed how every cut will be made.
items.host_open: Vienna’s cultural scene is facing a tighter budget. What do you think the city should protect first?

items.title: Fuel Price Rules Face Change
items.gist: Austria’s fuel-price measures are due to expire soon, but the government is divided on what should replace them. The economics minister has now proposed ending one key part.
items.summary: Austria’s current fuel-price measure is due to end in a few days. The governing parties disagree over whether to limit oil companies’ profit margins. Economics Minister Wolfgang Hattmannsdorfer said he wants that margin limit to end. He proposed continuing a reduction in mineral oil tax instead. He said there was no longer a need for the margin measure to protect supply. The government said it would provide more details before the end of November.
items.host_open: Austria’s fuel-price rules may soon take a different shape. How does that look from your perspective?

items.title: Ukraine Warns of Power Grid Attack
items.gist: Ukraine’s president says Russia may be preparing a major strike on vital systems. The warning comes as US-mediated talks continue without agreement on territory.
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia was preparing another major attack on Ukraine. He said energy systems, logistics and other critical services could be targeted. Russia has not publicly confirmed the reported plan. US envoy Jared Kushner said he believes Russian President Vladimir Putin wants peace. Kushner also said the talks had reached a deadlock over Ukrainian territory. The warning matters because attacks on energy systems can disrupt heat and electricity during winter.
items.host_open: Ukraine faces another serious threat to essential services. How does this warning make you feel?

items.title: Gaza Strikes Kill Ten
items.gist: Israeli strikes killed at least ten people in Gaza, according to reports. The latest violence is unfolding despite a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas.
items.summary: Israeli strikes killed at least ten people in Gaza, according to the Associated Press. Israel said its military killed a Hamas official who handled economic and education affairs. Gaza’s authorities reported the deaths. The strikes are part of continuing violence more than a year after a ceasefire deal began. The fighting has caused a severe humanitarian crisis for people in Gaza. The claims in the report could not all be independently verified.
items.host_open: Another night of strikes has brought loss and fear in Gaza. What is your reaction to this news?

items.title: Iraqi Kurds Protest Federal Takeover
items.gist: Thousands protested in Irbil over Baghdad’s plans for oil and border crossings. The dispute puts regional control and national authority in focus.
items.summary: Thousands of people protested in Irbil, the capital of Iraq’s Kurdish region. They opposed plans by Iraq’s federal government to take control of oil operations and border crossings. These areas have been managed by Kurdish authorities. Baghdad says it is asserting federal control. Kurdish leaders and protesters object to the proposed changes. The dispute could affect oil revenues and relations between the region and the central government.
items.host_open: A dispute over oil and borders has brought crowds into Irbil. What do you think is at stake for the region?

items.title: EU Leaders Debate Long-Term Budget
items.gist: European leaders met in Brussels to discuss the bloc’s next long-term budget and Ukraine’s financing needs. Several governments remain divided over the proposals.
items.summary: EU leaders met in Brussels on Thursday and Friday for a special summit. They are discussing the EU’s next long-term budget and financing for Ukraine in 2027. The talks aim to bring governments closer to agreement. Some member states object to the proposals on the table. The budget will shape spending on security, competitiveness and other shared priorities. No final agreement was reported at the start of the summit.
items.host_open: The EU’s next budget will shape priorities for years. Which issue do you think deserves most attention?

items.title: Spain’s Far Right Seeks Power
items.gist: Spain votes on Sunday, with immigration fears helping the far-right Vox party attract support. The election could reshape the country’s politics.
items.summary: Spain is due to hold a national election on Sunday, November 29. The far-right Vox party is campaigning on immigration and national identity. It says that Spanish citizens should come before foreign residents and immigrants. Some voters say they support Vox for its defence of Spain’s Catholic roots. Vox has not governed nationally since the Franco era. The result could affect the balance of power in Madrid.
items.host_open: Spain is heading into a closely watched election. How do you think immigration will shape the result?

items.title: Judge Blocks ABC License Review
items.gist: A US judge stopped the regulator from starting an early review of ABC station licenses. The network said the review could chill its speech.
items.summary: A federal judge blocked the Federal Communications Commission from an early review of ABC broadcast licenses. The ruling came after ABC challenged the regulator’s action. The network argued that the move could restrict its freedom of speech. The FCC is an independent US agency that regulates broadcasting. The administration has disputed ABC in a wider conflict with news outlets. The case is part of ongoing legal battles over media access and government power.
items.host_open: A court has put a pause on a high-profile media dispute. How do you feel about that?

items.title: Lukoil Assets Draw US-Led Bid
items.gist: A consortium including a US government lender agreed to acquire Lukoil’s overseas energy assets. Critics say the arrangement raises questions about sanctions and public money.
items.summary: A consortium led by US investment firm Eldridge agreed to acquire Lukoil International. The company owns energy assets in 11 countries, including oil and gas fields and refineries. The group includes a US government lender and companies from the United Arab Emirates and the United States. The proposed deal would use restricted Russian shares rather than direct cash payments to Russia. A US lawmaker criticized the government lender’s involvement. The deal is linked to sanctions imposed on Russian energy companies over the war in Ukraine.
items.host_open: A proposed oil deal is raising questions about sanctions and public finance. What stands out to you?

items.title: NASA’s Voyager Reaches One Light-Day
items.gist: Voyager 1 has reached a remarkable distance from Earth, nearly fifty years after launch. The milestone shows how long a spacecraft can keep travelling.
items.summary: NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft reached a distance of one light-day from Earth on November 18. That is about 25.9 billion kilometres. The spacecraft launched in 1977 and has travelled through space for nearly five decades. A light-day is the distance light travels in one day. Voyager continues to send information from far beyond the planets. Its journey remains a landmark in space exploration.
items.host_open: Voyager 1 has travelled farther than most of us can picture. Did that surprise you?

items.title: Book Wien Opens Its Doors
items.gist: Vienna’s major book fair began with a public opening on Wednesday evening. Readers can meet writers and researchers through Sunday.
items.summary: The Buch Wien book fair opened in Vienna on Wednesday evening. Publicist Michel Friedman took part in the opening. The programme runs until Sunday, November 29. Guests include prize-winning author Elias Hirschl and bestselling writer Marc Elsberg. Extremism researcher Julia Ebner is also on the programme. The fair brings authors, readers and current debates together in one place.
items.host_open: Vienna’s book fair has turned the city into a meeting place for readers. Which kind of book event do you enjoy most?

items.title: A 400,000-Guest Wedding
items.gist: A wedding celebration in India drew an enormous crowd and brought traffic to a standstill. A planned horse race had to be postponed after tens of thousands arrived.
items.summary: A wedding celebration in Bihar, India, drew an estimated 400,000 guests. The host was politician Anant Singh, who invited local residents as well as public figures. Roads near the event became heavily congested. Organisers prepared a large vegetarian meal and hundreds of thousands of sweets. A horse race planned as part of the celebration was delayed after around 100,000 people gathered to watch. The event drew attention for its huge scale and the disruption it caused.
items.host_open: This wedding needed a crowd plan on a remarkable scale. What was your first reaction to those numbers?
